mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over the past month signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales of 1% or more over the past two months indicates weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where RSAFS declines > 1% in the prior two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals labor market distress, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases > 1% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in one month, it signals a mismatch between monetary policy and inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past two months, coupled with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points, signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% in 2 months and UNRATE declines > 0.2pp
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST increases > 5% and UNRATE declines > 0.2pp in the prior two months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) relative to its 12-month moving average indicates strong labor market conditions, which typically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.25% in one month, it signals a restrictive monetary policy, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases > 0.25% in the prior month.
